month_3_projection: Scales linearly with revenue.
month_6_projection: Still not a strategic concern unless pricing is very low and churn is high.
recommendation: Treat as normal SaaS variable cost.

current_state: Internal scan worker is capped at 5 minutes on Vercel.
month_3_projection: At moderate usage this becomes a reliability problem before it becomes a cloud-cost problem.
month_6_projection: By month 6, serious API usage will force worker offloading or queue-based background execution.
recommendation: Move scanning to dedicated workers or jobs before pushing hard on heavy API-led acquisition.
notes: This is a code-derived constraint, not an external source.

current_state: Pages and outbound links are processed serially, with explicit pacing and retries.
month_3_projection: Moderate scans will finish, but larger scans will stretch or fail under current worker limits.
month_6_projection: Large sites and heavy agency use will not feel infrastructure-grade until concurrency and queueing improve.
recommendation: Add queueing, chunked scans, and resumable jobs.
notes: Good for safety, bad for throughput.

current_state: Crawler uses 500ms page delay and 1s per-domain pacing, and records 429 domains. This helps but does not eliminate blocking risk.
month_3_projection: As usage grows, repeated checks from the same egress IPs will draw more blocks.
month_6_projection: By month 6, IP rotation, proxy strategy, or browser fallback for premium checks may be needed.
recommendation: Plan for scanner egress control before scale, not after.
notes: Good first layer, not a long-term moat.

current_state: Agency currently allows 1000 API read requests per hour, and each check-links request can contain 20 URLs.
month_3_projection: By month 3, one serious customer can push a meaningful amount of network work even without full-site scans.
month_6_projection: By month 6, this should be tied to usage credits, not just request count.
recommendation: Meter by URLs checked or link checks consumed, not just API calls.
notes: 20,000 URL checks per hour is possible on current limits.

current_state: Tier config includes monthly crawl page limits, but enforcement was not found in the active code paths reviewed.
month_3_projection: This leaves margin exposed if customers use high-frequency scans heavily.
month_6_projection: By month 6, this becomes a pricing and reliability problem if not enforced.
recommendation: Enforce monthly crawl pages and consider overage billing.
notes: Important gap between pricing design and implementation.

current_state: Per-scan webhook_url is accepted in API scan requests but appears only to be logged, not delivered as an actual callback.
month_3_projection: This can create developer trust issues if documented behavior does not match runtime behavior.
month_6_projection: By month 6, fixing this is table stakes for API credibility.
recommendation: Fix before making API the headline feature.
notes: General account webhooks exist; per-scan callback path looks incomplete.
